reason: A vague count with no number ('branches usually not numerous'); the count-of-parts pattern needs a number, and the previous review rejected 'few' and 'many'.
Negation of PATO_0104365 plicate (EXACT synonym pleated), as 'unlobed' = not lobed.

'Stems remotely branched' means the branches are widely spaced along the stem: FLOPO:0991189 distant, borne by the branches (PO_0025073) of the stem. The word does not name a separate kind of branching.
Endostome sticking to the exostome without being fused: FLOPO:0991188 adherent. 'Weakly' only grades it, and the other part ('to the exostome') goes through docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.
Says the plant has no red tinge: negation of PATO_0000322 red.
States that the stem or plant has no rhizoids; PO_0030078 rhizoid exists.

label: xerochastic
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening when dry and closing when moist. NOTE: Opposite of hygrochastic; in mosses said of the peristome, in seed plants of fruits.
reason: French 'xérochastique' (misspelt): a real botanical term with no PATO or FLOPO class. Its parent is not a perfect fit, because a peristome opens rather than dehisces.

Two values that both hold, not a range between them: triangular (PATO_0001875, EXACT synonym deltoid) and a short sharp point at the apex (apiculate; PATO has it only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness, PATO_0000944).
Stems and branches thickly set with leaves: FLOPO:0991012 leafy ('densely' is a degree). The bearer is the stem or branch, not the leaf.
Two values that both hold for the hyaline cells: PATO_0001938 rhomboid and PATO_0001154 elongated. No term is needed.
'Leaf cells with large lumens' means the lumen of the cell is large: PATO_0000586 increased size, borne by the lumen as a part of the cell.
'Microphyllous branches' bear small, reduced leaves: PATO_0000587 decreased size, borne by the leaves (PO_0025034) of the branch, not by the branch itself.

Said of the pores of hyaline cells, which have no PO class and are wrongly attached to the leaf here. There is no 'ringed' (pore with a thickened rim) term to negate; PATO_0002539 ring shaped is a shape.
Negation of PATO_0001359 rugose.
There is no unary 'arranged in rows' term to negate: PATO_0001653 aligned with needs a second part, and FLOPO uniseriate/biseriate count the rows. Too few statements to justify a new class.
Incrassate cells are thick-walled, so 'not incrassate' negates PATO_0000591 increased thickness, borne by the cell wall. That is weaker than 'thin-walled' (PATO_0000592).
A hyphenated shape between ovoid (PATO_0001891 ovate, EXACT synonym ovoid) and PATO_0001873 cylindrical. It is a continuum, like 'linear-lanceolate'.
The ends of the leaf cells stick out as spine-like points on the back of the leaf: PATO_0001365 spiny, on the dorsal surface. 'Prorate' is a rare moss word, not worth its own class.
Small teeth that end in spinules: PATO_0001205 dentated (toothed) together with PATO_0001365 spiny. Two values that both hold, not a range.
The Y-mark is the three-armed scar on a spore, a part rather than a quality, and it has no PO class. The statements describe how visible or raised it is.
A margin finely scalloped by papillae: PATO_0001889 scalloped (synonym crenulate) together with FLOPO:0991059 papillose.
Cymbiform = boat-shaped = PATO_0002426 scaphoid (previous rule C215); this is its negation.
Negation of FLOPO:0991059 papillose.
With several ribs: FLOPO:0991062 ribbed. 'Pluri-' gives no number, so the count-of-parts pattern does not apply.
'Markings' is vague (dots, streaks or raphide lines) and is listed beside raphide cells, so no single quality can be negated.

label: botuliform
definition: A cylindrical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongate, somewhat swollen and rounded at both ends, like a sausage. NOTE: Said of corollas and buds (e.g. Loranthaceae); allantoid adds a slight curvature.
reason: A real botanical shape term with no PATO or FLOPO class; cylindrical is the nearest parent.
Bearing bulbils; bulbil is a synonym of PO_0004548 aerial tuber.
A continuum between ovoid (PATO_0001891) and ellipsoid (PATO_0000947), plus a separate flattened value (PATO_0002254). No term is needed.
'Disc florets/flowers' are disk flowers; disc floret is a synonym of PO_0025332.
A broken transcription. The examples are ordinary 'pubescent' (PATO_0000455) with a position, which the existing rules already handle.
